systems.platform: mobile app, built by the Force ICT Department with financial-sector stakeholders
systems.tiers: national, public-facing; launched 1 September 2026; the public reports suspected financial fraud, uploads evidence, tracks cases and gets feedback; police sources told the outlet they had not heard of it

systems.platform: developed by Web Assets Nigeria Limited with other technology partners
systems.tiers: anonymous crime reporting by video, voice or text; launched 2017, piloted in the Federal Capital Territory; reported largely defunct by 2019

systems.platform: mobile app, more than 100,000 downloads on Google Play
systems.tiers: introduced 2021; emergency alerts and crime reporting to the Police Command and Control unit; more than 10,000 fake alerts reported by March 2022; still available in September 2026, though the writer's registration code never arrived

systems.owner: Nigeria Police Force National Cybercrime Centre
systems.tiers: the public submits cybercrime reports, uploads evidence and tracks cases; the centre describes it as operating 24/7 across all 36 states and reports more than 146,000 reports filed and more than N58 billion recovered

note: Four police platforms through which the public reports: public class, and the cybercrime portal is also limited to one class of offence. None is a record the station makes when it takes a report, so no fact.
